comment: CANONICAL coding-rule set for the tracked RTL under test (rtl/, the single normative tree). Run by lint/check_rules.py; wired into the per-module gate. 25 rules: 3 tool-driven (verilator x2, iverilog x1) and 22 source-level checks that encode the WP section 6 / LINT.md conventions. Each rule is machine-checked and fails loudly; none of them may be weakened to make a gate pass.

rules.text: Verilator lint exits 0: no %Error line
only the recorded style warning classes fire (UNUSEDSIGNAL, UNUSEDPARAM)
Icarus compile exits 0; Icarus 'sorry:' limitation notes are not violations
no initial blocks in synthesizable RTL
no delay controls (#) in synthesizable RTL
no fork/join in synthesizable RTL
no casez/casex: use a plain case with explicit 4-state semantics
no procedural force/release/deassign on a variable
no simulation-only system tasks in synthesizable RTL
no real/realtime types in synthesizable RTL
no disable of a named block in synthesizable RTL
no legacy always @* / always @(posedge): use always_ff / always_comb
no reg declarations: use logic
every sequential process uses always_ff (present in each RTL module)
no non-blocking assignment inside an always_comb block
no blocking assignment inside an always_ff block (sequential logic must use non-blocking)
every sequential process has an explicit asynchronous reset branch (if (!rst_n))
no port without an explicit data type
no output port without an explicit data type
every file has an include guard (`ifndef) so a package/module is included at most once
no 4-state `bit` storage: use logic for synthesizable state
no unresolved TODO/FIXME/XXX/HACK markers in the RTL under test
every RTL module imports the single source of truth (tile_pkg) for its widths and encodings
no CRLF line endings: the RTL is LF-only
no wait/expect statements in synthesizable RTL
